model_annotation: The graph illustrates the performance of three different methods—Teacher, Self-Training, and PST—measured by their F1 scores as a function of the label rate, which ranges from 0 to 0.585 on a linear scale. The y-axis represents the F1 score, with values ranging from 52.5 to 72.5. Each method is represented by a distinct line: the Teacher method is shown as a red line with circular markers, the Self-Training method as a blue line with square markers, and the PST method as a green line with circular markers. All three lines exhibit a general downward trend as the label rate increases. At a label rate of 0, the Teacher method achieves the highest F1 score, approximately 72.2, followed by the PST method at around 71.8, and the Self-Training method at about 70.3. As the label rate increases, the F1 scores for all methods decrease, with the Teacher method showing the most significant drop, reaching approximately 52.5 at a label rate of 0.585. The Self-Training method maintains a relatively higher F1 score compared to the Teacher method at higher label rates, while the PST method shows a steady decline but remains above the other two methods until the label rate reaches 0.5, after which it drops sharply.
